Alex / BlueHarbor procurement —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier this week. Attached is a draft mutual action plan (MAP) and an evaluation checklist that should help move the AWS Private Offer route through procurement while we run the evaluation on Redwood Dedicated. High-level asks:

- Can you confirm whether procurement prefers Marketplace (AWS Private Offer) billing or a direct invoice from Redwood? Both are possible, we just need to know which accounts/contacts to route.
- Target close window: BlueHarbor indicated end-of-month cadence — can we aim to have contractual acceptance + PO by 2026-11-25 so we can allocate dedicated capacity in early Dec?
- Please review the attached MAP (BlueHarbor_MAP_v1.xlsx) and flag any missing milestones (vendor forms, security attestation, PO format).

Draft MAP highlights (summary):
- Week 1 (now): sandbox access + initial perf tests (Redwood provides ephemeral sandbox)
- Week 2: procurement review & PO issuance (BlueHarbor)
- Week 3: AWS Private Offer created by Redwood and accepted by BlueHarbor
- Week 4: provision Dedicated capacity and onboarding runbooks

Attachments: BlueHarbor_MAP_v1.xlsx, PO_Template_BlueHarbor.pdf, AWS_Private_Offer_Link.txt

If this looks good I can loop in our billing lead (Rachel) and our sales engineer (Karthik) to confirm the billing flow and technical acceptance criteria.

Thanks,

Ben —

Appreciate the MAP and checklist. A few quick procurement items before we can accept a private offer:

1) Preferred billing: our procurement team prefers AWS Marketplace (Private Offer) for SaaS vendors because it ties to our central billing account. That said, we sometimes accept direct vendor invoices for POs below $50k — we'll confirm thresholds.
2) Vendor forms: procurement will need a completed vendor setup packet (W-9, bank details, export compliance). Can Redwood provide a vendor packet or a link to your vendor form?
3) Quote: we need a formal quote that shows line-item pricing, effective start date, and payment terms (Net 30). Can you attach an official quote tied to the Private Offer flow?

Timeline: procurement review will take 5–7 business days once the quote + vendor packet are submitted. If we get everything by end of next week (2026-11-19) I think the 2026-11-25 target is doable but tight.

Also — can you confirm support for usage-based billing reconciliation via AWS invoices (we have an internal finance flow for marketplace charges)?

If you can loop Rachel and Karthik into the thread to confirm the quote format and onboarding steps that would be great.

—Alex

Thanks Alex — looping in the right folks from our side.

Quick answers up front:
- We support AWS Private Offer billing and the marketplace invoice flow. Redwood will create the Private Offer; once BlueHarbor accepts, AWS will handle invoicing to your billing account. Redwood can also provide a direct quote/invoice if procurement prefers that path.
- Vendor packet: Rachel, can you confirm we have a vendor packet PDF we can send? If not, we can provide a short vendor info form and W-9.
- Quote: I'll attach a formal quote (line items + start date) once we finalize the package below.

Recommended procurement steps (suggested):
1) Redwood issues formal quote and uploads vendor packet to your shared drive (Ben) — 1 business day
2) BlueHarbor procurement performs vendor validation & issues PO — 3–7 business days
3) Redwood creates AWS Private Offer and sends acceptance link to BlueHarbor — 1–2 business days after PO
4) BlueHarbor accepts Private Offer in AWS Marketplace, AWS handles billing going forward

If BlueHarbor wants the shorter path, we can accept a PO + direct invoice and skip the marketplace flow; however Private Offer gives consolidated billing and is preferable from your description.

Alex / team — quick technical plan and acceptance criteria from our side to make the evaluation deterministic. High level steps:

1) Sandbox access (Day 0–2): provide BlueHarbor a sandbox token + sample dataset (small subset). Redwood will enable a dedicated evaluation namespace and a pre-provisioned KV cache to mirror your production sequence lengths.
2) Performance baseline tests (Day 3–5): run 3 scripted workloads (chat latency, batch embedding throughput, and long-context generation). Acceptance criteria: median p50 latency <= 120ms for short chat (<=128 tokens), embedding throughput >= 250 reqs/sec for 1536-dim models.
3) Feature validation (Day 6–10): verify streaming, function-calling, and model rollbacks. Provide test prompts and scoring harness.
4) Billing/procurement handoff (parallel): once PO accepted, we provision the Dedicated GPU pool and finalize the private offer.

Artifacts I'll provide by Monday: evaluation checklist (inline below), test harness commands, and a DocuSign draft for the order form if you prefer signed acceptance.

Evaluation checklist (summary):
- Sandbox credentials + sample data (provided)
- Predefined perf tests + scoring script
- Success criteria document (pass/fail buckets)
- Runbook for scale tests + rollback plan

DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/signet/REDWOOD-BH-0097 (placeholder)
HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/DH-2026-BH-0097

Let me know any modifications to the perf targets — we can tune model variant and quantization to meet throughput/latency requirements.

Thanks,
